newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - June 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - June 2.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Monday:
* French Socialists and their Communist allies scored a solid victory in the second round of parliamentary elections.
* French President Jacques Chirac, who was dealt a severe blow with the latest round of elections, misread the nation's reservations about American-led economic reforms.
* There was an 11 percent drop in homicides in the United States in 1996, according to an FBI report.
* The widow of civil rights leader Malcolm X was severely burned in a fire in her home, and her 12-year-old grandson is deemed a suspect.
* The victims and relatives of those killed in the Oklahoma City bombing are enduring a difficult wait as jurors in the case entered their third day of deliberations.
* President Bill Clinton's lawyer said he may be willing to delve into accuser Paula Corbin Jones' sexual history if she pursues her sexual-harassment case.
* Three Democrats reach their final day of campaigning in their bid to win the right to face New Jersey Republican Gov. Christie Todd Whitman.
